r: **Seuna (Sevuna) Yadavas** of Devagiri; ruled the western Deccan (Maharashtra) c. **1187–1317**
First **feudatories of the Western (Kalyani) Chalukyas** (and earlier the Rashtrakutas)
**Marathi** – the Yadavas **encouraged Marathi**; **Sanskrit** = language of scholarship
**Bhillama V** – threw off Kalyani Chalukya rule and built **Devagiri** (c. **1187**) as capital
Name given to Devagiri by **Muhammad bin Tughlaq** when he shifted his capital there (**1327**)
Founder; built Devagiri; beaten by Hoysala Veera Ballala II
**Killed Kakatiya Rudradeva**; held young Ganapatideva captive, released him (1199) and married his daughter **Somaladevi** to him
**Greatest Yadava**; title **Teluguraya Sthapanacharya**; defeated the Hoysalas; son **Sarangapanideva** later served at Rudramadevi's court
His attack on the Kakatiyas was **repulsed by Rudramadevi**
Ruler at **Alauddin Khalji's 1296 raid**; later a vassal
**Jaitugi** – recorded by Hemadri and confirmed by the **Paithan copper plate** of Ramachandra
As a counterweight to Hoysala **Veera Ballala II's** push into the **Krishna–Tungabhadra** region

**First Muslim invasion of the South**: Alauddin Khalji, then governor of Kara under Sultan Jalaluddin, raids Devagiri and defeats **Ramachandra**; promised the yearly revenue of **Ellichpur** but did not send it
**Malik Kafur**: **Ramachandra** submits and is taken to Delhi, then restored as a vassal
**Malik Burhanuddin** of Devagiri given charge of Andhra; Devagiri = the Sultanate's Deccan base

2.x: **Significance:** Devagiri was the **first southern kingdom to fall** to Delhi and opened the road to Warangal, Dwarasamudra and Madurai.
